title: Elite Private Schools Offer Aid to Families Making $500,000
summary:
Private schools in the US are increasing financial aid and advertising discounts to attract students, as soaring tuition and a declining population of school-age children intensify competition.
Some schools, such as Brearley and Deerfield Academy, are offering free tuition to families earning under certain income thresholds, and using sliding scales to determine tuition for higher-earning families. Bloomberg's Erin Hudson joins Bloomberg's Intelligence to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Odd Lots: What’s Driving Africa’s Economic Growth?
summary:
Africa has seen lots of economic growth in the last few years. According to the United Nations, growth across the continent is expected to reach 4.0% in 2026.

Joe Studwell, author of How Africa Works: Success and Failure on the World's Last Developmental Frontier, joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal on the Odd Lots podcast to discuss what is driving this economic growth and how it compares to Asian counterparts. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Rise Before Nvidia’s Earnings as Oil Falls: Markets Wrap

title: European Stocks Rise as Pullback in Oil Lifts Investor Sentiment
summary: European stocks gained in a choppy trading session as a pullback in oil prices eased some of the inflation and bond-market pressures that have weighed on the region in recent days.

title: Bessent’s Mentor Druckenmiller Calls Bond Buying a Mistake
summary:
Stanley Druckenmiller, the billionaire investor who mentored US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in his early career as a hedge fund trader, suggested his former pupil is making a mistake by wading into the bond market.
Bessent has recently pledged to increase the Treasury’s purchases of long-dated bonds, a move widely seen as an attempt to push down yields in the world’s most important debt market.
Jason Trennert, Chairman and CEO at Strategas Research Partners, discusses US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's focus on yields and what to expect from Jackson Hole and the Fed. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Treasuries Gain as Oil Drop Eases Pressure on Inflation, Bessent

title: AI Revenue Slowdown Would Be the Market's Big Test
summary: Kelly Covley, senior investment analyst at Manning & Napier Advisors, says the market has become increasingly dependent on the AI trade, leaving stocks more vulnerable if demand begins to weaken. With AI spending now feeding through to industries across the economy, “the biggest test would be if you had a deceleration in revenue growth for the AI laboratories.” This interview aired Aug. 24, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Consumer Confidence Falls on Jobs, Business Outlook
summary: US consumer confidence fell in August to the worst since the start of the year as the Conference Board’s gauge of confidence decreased 0.8 points to 89.4 after a downward revision to the prior month. Michael McKee breaks down the data on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: VIX Curve ‘Bump’ Shows Stock-Market Anxiety Growing by Midterms
summary: While Nvidia Corp.’s upcoming earnings and Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s speech in Jackson Hole are the main events for investors this week, traders in the equity derivatives markets are already bracing for a potential uptick in volatility around the US midterm elections in November.

title: Apollo, IFM and KKR Said to Be Finalists in AB Ports Stake Sale
summary: Apollo Global Management, IFM Investors and KKR & Co. have reached the final round of bidding for a majority stake in Associated British Ports, the UK’s biggest port operator, according to people familiar with the matter.
